So I had envisioned setting up a program one time to run my dishwasher at 11PM every night but I've given up on that. Now I just run it when it's full and have no complaints about the quality of cleaning it performs. I just wish the people at Bosch had contacted some users to help write the instructions and programming. Then the user operation might be viable.

Sentence (English): Who knew you needed a light in your dishwasher?
Comments (English): [ Love the look, couple design changes ] || ---------------- || Who knew you needed a light in your dishwasher? The coolest feature ever and never going back! We now own two of these dishwashers one at home and one at our cabin. I love it. The third rack is fantastic and allows me to take the basket out during most washers to give me more space for larger items on bottom rack. In both of my dishwashers, the bottom rack rolls back in Its annoying when you are trying to load it and it keeps rolling back in. I have no idea why. I thought it was installed wrong until both did it and I know someone else that has one and theirs does it too. It's certainly usable but I don't understand why it won't stay open. Finally - the dry cycle needs some improvement. Depending on what it in the load, there can be a bit more than normal water remaining on items. They are not completely dry. Sentence (English): 14-Place vs. 12-Place Comparison / DUBJ1EP vs. DUE1BGL Comparison.
Comments (English): [ Comparison of 14-seater and 12-seater / Comparison with DUBJ1EP ] || ---------------- || 14-Place vs. 12-Place Comparison / DUBJ1EP vs. DUE1BGL Comparison. I previously used an LG 14-place dishwasher and switched to a 12-place model (my current one). Since I chose this product after much deliberation, I really wanted to leave a comparison review to help those who are considering purchasing one. Structure. As you know, the 14-place model has three tiers (top, top, and bottom), but this product (12-place) has only two tiers (top and bottom). This was the part that made me hesitate the most. Of course, it would be convenient to switch from a 12-place to a 14-place model, but for me, it's the opposite. However, the 14-place model costs in the 1 million won range, while the 12-place model is in the mid-600,000 won range. Since I'm only living in this house for a short time, I wanted to choose a cost-effective product rather than buying an expensive one. So, I decided to just use it first and get used to it even if it was inconvenient, and I chose this product. The conclusion is... drumroll... I am extremely satisfied. The biggest difference is that there is no top tier for cutlery and there is a separate cutlery holder, but this turned out to be much more convenient than I expected. I actually found this more convenient because I can put scissors, knives, and cutlery in a separate holder while washing, and then just lift the entire holder to take them out after the wash. When there are too many dishes, I don't use the separate holder; if I place the cutlery between the dishes, I can fit more dishes in the space where the holder used to be! Time. Even when I used the 14-place setting model, I rarely used the drying function. It took so long that I felt the electricity bill was a waste. This time, I skipped the drying function and ran it for the full cycle, and it took 1 hour and 39 minutes. (For reference, there is a 1-hour course, but I heard that uses more electricity). It has a top-loading quick cycle function, so it takes about 30 minutes when running only the top section—this is also very useful! Features. The cleaning power is, of course, excellent. It also has an automatic door opening feature, which is great. Comparison with DUBJ1EP. The overall functions are all similar. The DUBJ1EP is a 22-year-old model. The difference with the DUE1BGL is that it is a 24-year model that allows you to manage the dishwasher via your smartphone using the LG ThinQ app, and you can download custom features such as grilling meat, cooking fish, cleaning stubbornly stuck-on dishes, and handling wine glasses through the UP Appliance function! That is why I chose the DUE1BGL. Overall review: If you don't need a super high-end dishwasher, but want a 12-place setting capacity with most necessary features, good cleaning power, and an automatic door opening, then buy it. You won't regret it! If my review was helpful, please be sure to click "Helpful." Thank you.

Sentence (English): I bought the similar GE model but had to return it since the handle interfered with the neighboring drawer.
Comments (English): [ GE is Better ] || ---------------- || I bought the similar GE model but had to return it since the handle interfered with the neighboring drawer. This Whirlpool dishwasher is definitely sleek looking comparing it to other brands that don't have a handle. Other than the handle, the GE model is better in almost every way. The GE is over 10 pounds heavier which you can tell by the build material. The front of the GE is extremely sturdy and almost fingerprint proof. The whirlpool is extremely flimsy, feeling like a piece of plastic and it is NOT fingerprint proof. Your fingerprints will show after every use. The racks are not as sturdy as GE, the silverware cady is cheap and doesn't stay in its place, the GE buttons have more options and are aesthetically much nicer/modern, and the GE display screen is brighter. The door hinges seem to be either defective or poorly designed because you have to force the door open all of the way to access the bottom rack. This unit also occasionally squeaks while washing, again not sure if due to a product defect. Finally, GE has a built-in “garbage disposal” which means that you don't have to clean a filter every 3 months like with Whirlpool. After reading reviews on websites for this product, you'll quickly find out that Whirlpool has incentivized everybody who leaves a good review. Maybe the longevity is better? Guess only time will tell.

The brown vibration insulator had broken and this poor elbow was supporting most of the pump weight while being torqued in a second direction.  This is surely a recipe for disaster.I'm summary, I do like the unit, but it could use a little refinement.  I would still buy it again, assuming it's still made in the country I live.

The lower rack is a bot awkward, nothing seems to fit well in half of it as the pegs are very slanted and close together. There's an extra set of flip up pegs in this area but it doesn't solve the issue. Wish they were upright and further apart. The area doesn't work for plates because it's so slanted, pegs are too close together for bowls, and since its the bottom rack isnt great for big pots as it blocks the water flow. so nothing really fits there well. Cycle is long but does a good job. It's quiet. Feels well built and sturdy.

Sentence (English): Eighteen months in, we have totally enjoyed this dishwasher and have had no issues with it.
Comments (English): [ Running it twice a day for 18 months, no problems ] || ---------------- || Eighteen months in, we have totally enjoyed this dishwasher and have had no issues with it. We especially love how quiet it is and the very top rack for silverware. My only critique is that with the countertop, we can't see how much time it has left because the panel is hidden by the edge of the countertop. It has a few quiet beeps when it is done. We sometimes run the 60 minute cycle because it is already getting full and we'll have a bunch more dishes after the meal is done. We do periodically fill up the rinse agent when the indicator gives the notification. Generally everything gets clean even without rinsing beforehand through we dump food waste in organic recycling container before putting the dish in the dishwasher. Occasionally, we'll see a bowl that had caked on stuff (like chili) and was in a position that it still has specks of food on it and we'll put it through the dishwasher again. With three teenagers, after I prepare dinner, I will often run the dishwasher (with breakfast and lunch dishes and the dishes I got dirty making dinner). Then we will unload it after supper and then run it again overnight with the supper and evening snack dishes. I don't put nonstick pans through it but I often put glass cooking pans, cooling racks, and baking pans in there if I have room because I like to do the least hand washing that I have to. I also put all our kitchen knives through it because I don't want to wash them by hand even though the knife manufacturer recommends it (but yes then I need to periodically sharpen them because they get dull but they would get dull anyway). My point is that with three teenagers and not going out to eat often but making our own meals at home, this dishwasher is a great help.

Comments (English): [ So sleek and pretty and very efficient ] || ---------------- || I bought a new home and this brand dishwasher was already installed. However, I do love it. It works so good! I used the quick wash feature, thinking it was the best one for prerinsed dishes (I always prerinse my dishes), however, upon reading through the manual, I realized that this feature uses more water and energy than the normal (every day) wash! I wish that the owner's manual had more detailed instructions, because it only tells you how to install. There should be a detailed USER manual with each appliance. There's a dozen sheets online but none of them are really user friendly how-to's for an average person. But the most important thing is the overall function and it does a wonderful job! Don't forget to hit "restart" if you've opened the dishwasher up while it's drying, because it won't continue to go through the cycle process, even if you close the door.

The unit is very close to the floor with no room to work. The install guide instructs you to turn the unit on its back and install all the hoses before you slide the unit in place however it is still no enough room to work. I have worked on a lot of equipment in my lifetime and consider myself very mechanically inclined.

Sentence (English): The previous dishwasher, also Bosch, was about 18 years old, after reaching adulthood, we decided to give it a free pass.
Comments (English): [ It's OK, but.  ] || ---------------- || The previous dishwasher, also Bosch, was about 18 years old, after reaching adulthood, we decided to give it a free pass. During the previous one's use, it broke down a few times (minor injuries, towards the end of its life), most of which could be repaired with a screwdriver and cleaning the hoses. The new dishwasher, despite also being top-of-the-range, is louder, less capacious (height of the plates), the baskets seem weaker, generally, it gives the impression that it was designed not by an engineer, but by an accountant. Undoubtedly, it washes better than the old one (the dishwasher, of course), the plates are clean, they squeak. The length of the ECO program is irritating, but eco is not the same as convenience, oh well, such are the times. The application and remote start work perfectly. Adding the dishwasher to the app was painless. Although disappointed with the noise level, I recommend it.
Comments (Original): [ Jest OK, ale... ] || ---------------- || Poprzednia zmywarka, również Bosch, miala około 18 lat, po osiągnieciu pełnoletności, stwierdziliśmy, że dajemy jej wolną drogę...Podczas ekspoatacji poprzedniej, zepsuła się kilka razy (drobne urazy, pod koniec życia), większość można było naprawić przy pomocy śróbokręta i przeczyszczeniu węży.Nowa zmywarka, pomimo, iż jest również z górnej półki, jest głośniejsza, mniej pojemna (wysokość talerzy), kosze jakby słabsze, ogólnie, sprawia wrażenie zaprojektowanej nie przez inżyniera, ale księgowego...Bezsprzecznie, domywa lepiej niż stara (zmywarka oczywiście), talerze czyste, aż piszczą.Długość programu EKO jest irytująca, ale nie od dziś eko, nie równa się wcale wygoda, no cóż, takie czasy.Aplikacja i uruchamianie zdalne działa wzorowo.Dodanie zmywarki do apki, przebiegło bezboleśnie.Choć rozczarowany poziomem głośności, polecam.

Nice to meet you, Bespoke. ** Samsung Electronics Bespoke Kitchen Fit 14-seater Dishwasher ** I previously used a SK 6-seater dishwasher. Using it on the countertop made the kitchen space feel cramped, and the interior was more cramped than I expected, which was inconvenient. I was considering a 12-seater, but after hearing it could wash 16 more dishes, I ordered the 14-seater. I ordered the Glam White color to match my refrigerator, and it's even prettier in person. Using it was a whole new experience. It washes well and is incredibly quiet. I read other reviews before purchasing, and honestly, I thought it would be quieter, but it's truly amazing. And it has various wash cycles, so you can use it according to your needs. I give it high marks for its quiet yet powerful cleaning power. ^^ Prices fluctuate frequently, so be sure to check discount coupons and cart discounts before you buy. When I first ran it, there was still some moisture, perhaps because it hadn't dried enough. After drying it on auto mode, there was almost no moisture left. I heard that a strong dry cycle would remove even more moisture, but I haven't tried it yet. When the door opens automatically, I leave the water running a little longer and then clean up the pantry the next day. I run it once or twice a day, and it doesn't seem to affect my electricity bill as much as I thought. While the dishwasher is running, I play board games with the kids and help them with their homework. It's made my tiring evenings a little more fulfilling. I think it's a good choice for those who are struggling like I was. I'm very satisfied. I recommend it. I hope it helps.

Sentence (English): Finally, my wife has come to our house.
Comments (English): [ I support Bespoke, a great dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || Finally, my wife has come to our house. Nice to meet you, Bespoke. **Samsung Electronics Bespoke Kitchen Fit 14-seater dishwasher**. Before, I used a 6-seater SK dishwasher. Using it on the countertop made the kitchen space cramped, and the interior was more cramped than I expected, which was inconvenient. I was considering a 12-seater, but after hearing it could wash 16 more dishes, I ordered the 14-seater. I ordered the Glam White color to match my refrigerator, and it's even prettier in person. Using it was a whole new experience. It washes well and is incredibly quiet. I read other reviews before purchasing, but honestly, I thought it would be quieter, but it's truly amazing. And it has various wash cycles, so you can use it according to your needs. I give it high marks for its quiet yet powerful cleaning power. ^^ Prices fluctuate frequently, so be sure to check discount coupons and cart discounts before making a purchase. When I first ran it, there was still some moisture, perhaps because it hadn't dried enough. After drying it on auto mode, there was barely any moisture left. They say that if you power-dry, there's less moisture, but I haven't tried it yet. When the door opens automatically, I leave the water in a little longer and then organize the dishes in the cupboard the next day. I run it once or twice a day, and it doesn't seem to affect my electricity bill as much as I thought. While the dishwasher is running, I play board games with the kids and help them with their homework. It's made my tiring evenings a little more fulfilling. I think it's a good choice for those who are struggling like I was. I'm very satisfied. I recommend it. I hope it helps.
Comments (Original): [ 너무 좋은 식기세척기 비스포크 응원합니다 ] || ---------------- || 드디어 저희집에도 여사님 오셨어요. 반가워요 비스포크** 삼성전자 비스포크 키친핏 식기세척기 14인용 **그전에는 sk 6인용 식기세척기를 사용했어요. 상판 위에도 놓고 사용하니 주방 공간이 좁아지고, 생각보다 내부 공간이 좁아서 불편했어요..12인용을 살까 고민했는데 16개 이상 그릇이 더 세척된다는 말에 14인용으로 주문했습니다.색상은 저희집 냉장고 색상과 같게 글램화이트 주문했는데 실물이 더 이쁩니다.사용해보니 정말 신세계입니다. 잘 세척되고 너무 조용합니다. 구매 전 다른 후기를 보니 조용하다고 하시던데 솔직히 그래도 나겠지 생각했는데 정말 조용해요..정말 놀라워요.그리고 다양한 세척 코스가 있어서 상황에 맞게 사용가능합니다.조용하지만 강력한 세척력에 높은 점수를 주고 싶어요^^가격은 수시로 변동되니 할인쿠폰이랑 카트할인 잘 보시고 구매하세요.처음돌렸을때 건조가 조금 덜 되었는지 물기가 남아있더라구요. 자동으로 설정한 후 건조하니 물기가 거의 없었습니다. 강력건조하면 더 물기가 없다고 하는데 아직 사용안해봤어요.저절로 문이 열리면 저는 조금 더 물을 열어두고 다음날 식기장에 정리합니다.하루에 1번 많게는 2번정도 돌리는데 생각보다 전기료 변화가 없는 것 같아요.식기세척기 돌리는 동안 아이들과 보드게임도 하고 숙제도 봐주고 합니다.그동안 지쳤던 저녁 시간을 조금더 풍요롭게 만들어주었어요..저처럼 고민하시는분들 선택하셔도 좋을 것 같아요.저는 매우 만족합니다. 추천드려요.  도움되시길 바랍니다.

Sentence (English): Homemakers, why aren't you buying this?
Comments (English): [ #Why did I buy this now? #A new world has opened ] || ---------------- || Homemakers, why aren't you buying this? As a newlywed for a year, I used to want to enjoy a meal served on pretty tableware—like a beautiful rice cake that looks great—but I gave up on that idea every time I worried about the pile of dishes. While preparing for our move, my husband and I discussed it and decided to buy a 12-place setting model. Before buying, I even went to LG Best Shop to get a quote, but Coupang was the cheapest and even offered immediate delivery on the date I wanted. At first, a model that was 30,000 won cheaper came up, so I wondered what the difference was. I was told this model has one more cycle, so I figured the more expensive one would be better and chose it. The technician was so kind; he took care of the base cabinet neatly and installed it perfectly. The installation took about an hour, but after it was all done, he explained everything and taught me all the maintenance tips, so I had no worries at all. The dishwasher was installed so beautifully, looking as if it was custom-made for me. I put in the detergent I had bought in advance and ran a cycle right away that evening, and I wonder if washing dishes is ever this easy? Since it's hot these days and I always wash dishes with hot water, I used to sweat a lot, so I used to feel a bit down thinking about the dishes after meals, but that feeling completely vanished. I give it a quick rinse with water and hand it to my husband. He plays Tetris with it, presses the power button, and sets it to 1 hour plus high-temperature drying—that's it! The door even opens automatically when it's finished! (You absolutely have to buy this). I won't have to worry when guests come over, and I feel like my housework worries have decreased significantly even after having a child, so I think this might be the best choice I've ever made. If you're still hesitating, you're just wasting your time! Housewives, breathe a sigh of relief after purchasing a dishwasher that cleans better than hand washing. Highly, highly recommended!

Sentence (English): Housewives, breathe a sigh of relief after purchasing a dishwasher that cleans better than hand washing.
Comments (English): [ #Why did I buy this now? #A new world has opened ] || ---------------- || Homemakers, why aren't you buying this? As a newlywed for a year, I used to want to enjoy a meal served on pretty tableware—like a beautiful rice cake that looks great—but I gave up on that idea every time I worried about the pile of dishes. While preparing for our move, my husband and I discussed it and decided to buy a 12-place setting model. Before buying, I even went to LG Best Shop to get a quote, but Coupang was the cheapest and even offered immediate delivery on the date I wanted. At first, a model that was 30,000 won cheaper came up, so I wondered what the difference was. I was told this model has one more cycle, so I figured the more expensive one would be better and chose it. The technician was so kind; he took care of the base cabinet neatly and installed it perfectly. The installation took about an hour, but after it was all done, he explained everything and taught me all the maintenance tips, so I had no worries at all. The dishwasher was installed so beautifully, looking as if it was custom-made for me. I put in the detergent I had bought in advance and ran a cycle right away that evening, and I wonder if washing dishes is ever this easy? Since it's hot these days and I always wash dishes with hot water, I used to sweat a lot, so I used to feel a bit down thinking about the dishes after meals, but that feeling completely vanished. I give it a quick rinse with water and hand it to my husband. He plays Tetris with it, presses the power button, and sets it to 1 hour plus high-temperature drying—that's it! The door even opens automatically when it's finished! (You absolutely have to buy this). I won't have to worry when guests come over, and I feel like my housework worries have decreased significantly even after having a child, so I think this might be the best choice I've ever made. If you're still hesitating, you're just wasting your time! Housewives, breathe a sigh of relief after purchasing a dishwasher that cleans better than hand washing. Highly, highly recommended!

Sentence (English): Great dishwasher for plates and silverware.
Comments (English): [ Good cleaning, not a fan of the racks ] || ---------------- || Great dishwasher for plates and silverware. Not great if you use bowls, cups, cooking utensils, serving pieces, and wine glasses. After a month, I have not yet found a logical place for cereal bowls, serving bowls/dishes or any round or deep item, unless I dedicate a load to running just a few items laying across the entire rack space. The middle (cup/bowl) rack makes no sense at all. The tines are too slanted to stabilize any glasses and the wine glass racks do not align with the racks/tines; the wine glass holders do nothing but take up space. (To be fair, the same was true about the wine glass holders for my old Whirlpool, so I just removed them.) I can load about 3 cereal bowls if I want to save a couple of rows for cups, unless I am willing to stack them on top of each other and risk broken dishes. The rack is too shallow and the tine configuration cannot hold up any bowls in a vertical or slanted position; the bowls just kind of lay there take up most of the rack.The lower rack tines closest to the door are good if you use the adjustable tines, but only for plates. Otherwise, they can only hold a single bowl laying on top of the tines. Serving bowls/dishes have no where to go except laying flat face down over the tines, each taking up 1/4 to 1/3 o the lower rack. Trying to stand them up requires leaning the bowls back on tines in a 6 inch opening between the rows of tines; this positions the bowls at an angle which results in collecting dirty water. The tines are too short, too slanted and too poorly positioned to serve any useful purpose for anything other than plates and shallow pasta bowls. Plates are where this thing excels. We have relatively flat plates which fit very nicely in the lower rear rack and in the lower front rack using the adjustable tines. Very shallow pasta bowls do pretty well, too. You can fit a lot and these things always come out spotless.The upper rack for silverware gets the job done, though it takes more attention to load than a basket. If you are thoughtful about positioning items, you can load a lot of silverware and it gets cleaner than in the basket. However, my family has not yet noticed (and ignored my instructions) that the front area of the upper rack has wider spacing; they frequently put spoons there which flop over facing upwards and collect dirty water during the cycle.The bottom rack utensil basket is too shallow to hold anything that does not fit in the top rack; items just fall over into the bottom. I have only used it once or twice; it mostly just sits there empty and takes up space. However, the space is pretty useless anyway since it is just a big wide channel on the side of the rack. It smells pretty bad by the end of the day after loading dishes all day to run over night. This did not happen with our 2 previous Whirlpools. However, the filter is pretty easy to clean, though that does little to address the smell. The auto open feature is nice. Everything is dry and cool to the touch after a short drying period (except, of course, coffee mugs and things with deep rims that trap small pools of water, which is to be expected with any dishwasher).If you're into dishwasher apps on your phone, this one seems to be okay. No games or cool graphics or sounds, but lots of VERY interesting information about your dishwasher. I don't know how I ever functioned without knowing the average monthly power and water consumption for my appliance! I personally can't see the benefit of moving essential functions like delay start off the machine's control panel to a separate device, but I guess that's "progress."It is very quiet, it does clean whatever you are able to get into it, and it looks nice.

Not great if you use bowls, cups, cooking utensils, serving pieces, and wine glasses. After a month, I have not yet found a logical place for cereal bowls, serving bowls/dishes or any round or deep item, unless I dedicate a load to running just a few items laying across the entire rack space. The middle (cup/bowl) rack makes no sense at all. The tines are too slanted to stabilize any glasses and the wine glass racks do not align with the racks/tines; the wine glass holders do nothing but take up space. (To be fair, the same was true about the wine glass holders for my old Whirlpool, so I just removed them.) I can load about 3 cereal bowls if I want to save a couple of rows for cups, unless I am willing to stack them on top of each other and risk broken dishes. The rack is too shallow and the tine configuration cannot hold up any bowls in a vertical or slanted position; the bowls just kind of lay there take up most of the rack.The lower rack tines closest to the door are good if you use the adjustable tines, but only for plates. Otherwise, they can only hold a single bowl laying on top of the tines. Serving bowls/dishes have no where to go except laying flat face down over the tines, each taking up 1/4 to 1/3 o the lower rack. Trying to stand them up requires leaning the bowls back on tines in a 6 inch opening between the rows of tines; this positions the bowls at an angle which results in collecting dirty water. The tines are too short, too slanted and too poorly positioned to serve any useful purpose for anything other than plates and shallow pasta bowls. Plates are where this thing excels. We have relatively flat plates which fit very nicely in the lower rear rack and in the lower front rack using the adjustable tines. Very shallow pasta bowls do pretty well, too. You can fit a lot and these things always come out spotless.The upper rack for silverware gets the job done, though it takes more attention to load than a basket. If you are thoughtful about positioning items, you can load a lot of silverware and it gets cleaner than in the basket. However, my family has not yet noticed (and ignored my instructions) that the front area of the upper rack has wider spacing; they frequently put spoons there which flop over facing upwards and collect dirty water during the cycle.The bottom rack utensil basket is too shallow to hold anything that does not fit in the top rack; items just fall over into the bottom. I have only used it once or twice; it mostly just sits there empty and takes up space. However, the space is pretty useless anyway since it is just a big wide channel on the side of the rack. It smells pretty bad by the end of the day after loading dishes all day to run over night. This did not happen with our 2 previous Whirlpools. However, the filter is pretty easy to clean, though that does little to address the smell. The auto open feature is nice. Everything is dry and cool to the touch after a short drying period (except, of course, coffee mugs and things with deep rims that trap small pools of water, which is to be expected with any dishwasher).If you're into dishwasher apps on your phone, this one seems to be okay. No games or cool graphics or sounds, but lots of VERY interesting information about your dishwasher. I don't know how I ever functioned without knowing the average monthly power and water consumption for my appliance! I personally can't see the benefit of moving essential functions like delay start off the machine's control panel to a separate device, but I guess that's "progress."It is very quiet, it does clean whatever you are able to get into it, and it looks nice.

But then, the next 9 washes had issues, with food left on bowls and silverware, and the 3rd rack not cleaning the serving spoons like it did the first few times. In one case, we had a spoon that was used to add a dollop of sour cream to a dish, and after washing it (with steam on), the sour cream baked onto the spoon. It could be that some things shouldn't have steam, it would be nice if GE published a guide of the best washer options based on what kinds of things and debris is being washed, and I'm sure their resource teams have this information. But in any case, for some reason it's not as good as it was during the 7-day evaluation period, which is disappointing. This is using the recommended Cascade packets and rinse.The noise level is great, and plates have gotten clean in all loads.

Sentence (English): Great dishwasher for plates and silverware.
Comments (English): [ Good cleaning, not a fan of the racks ] || ---------------- || Great dishwasher for plates and silverware. Not great if you use bowls, cups, cooking utensils, serving pieces, and wine glasses. After a month, I have not yet found a logical place for cereal bowls, serving bowls/dishes or any round or deep item, unless I dedicate a load to running just a few items laying across the entire rack space. The middle (cup/bowl) rack makes no sense at all. The tines are too slanted to stabilize any glasses and the wine glass racks do not align with the racks/tines; the wine glass holders do nothing but take up space. (To be fair, the same was true about the wine glass holders for my old Whirlpool, so I just removed them.) I can load about 3 cereal bowls if I want to save a couple of rows for cups, unless I am willing to stack them on top of each other and risk broken dishes. The rack is too shallow and the tine configuration cannot hold up any bowls in a vertical or slanted position; the bowls just kind of lay there take up most of the rack. The lower rack tines closest to the door are good if you use the adjustable tines, but only for plates. Otherwise, they can only hold a single bowl laying on top of the tines. Serving bowls/dishes have no where to go except laying flat face down over the tines, each taking up 1/4 to 1/3 o the lower rack. Trying to stand them up requires leaning the bowls back on tines in a 6 inch opening between the rows of tines; this positions the bowls at an angle which results in collecting dirty water. The tines are too short, too slanted and too poorly positioned to serve any useful purpose for anything other than plates and shallow pasta bowls. Plates are where this thing excels. We have relatively flat plates which fit very nicely in the lower rear rack and in the lower front rack using the adjustable tines. Very shallow pasta bowls do pretty well, too. You can fit a lot and these things always come out spotless. The upper rack for silverware gets the job done, though it takes more attention to load than a basket. If you are thoughtful about positioning items, you can load a lot of silverware and it gets cleaner than in the basket. However, my family has not yet noticed (and ignored my instructions) that the front area of the upper rack has wider spacing; they frequently put spoons there which flop over facing upwards and collect dirty water during the cycle. The bottom rack utensil basket is too shallow to hold anything that does not fit in the top rack; items just fall over into the bottom. I have only used it once or twice; it mostly just sits there empty and takes up space. However, the space is pretty useless anyway since it is just a big wide channel on the side of the rack. It smells pretty bad by the end of the day after loading dishes all day to run over night. This did not happen with our 2 previous Whirlpools. However, the filter is pretty easy to clean, though that does little to address the smell. The auto open feature is nice. Everything is dry and cool to the touch after a short drying period (except, of course, coffee mugs and things with deep rims that trap small pools of water, which is to be expected with any dishwasher). If you're into dishwasher apps on your phone, this one seems to be okay. No games or cool graphics or sounds, but lots of VERY interesting information about your dishwasher. I don't know how I ever functioned without knowing the average monthly power and water consumption for my appliance! I personally can't see the benefit of moving essential functions like delay start off the machine's control panel to a separate device, but I guess that's \"progress.\". It is very quiet, it does clean whatever you are able to get into it, and it looks nice.

I can load about 3 cereal bowls if I want to save a couple of rows for cups, unless I am willing to stack them on top of each other and risk broken dishes. The rack is too shallow and the tine configuration cannot hold up any bowls in a vertical or slanted position; the bowls just kind of lay there take up most of the rack.The lower rack tines closest to the door are good if you use the adjustable tines, but only for plates. Otherwise, they can only hold a single bowl laying on top of the tines. Serving bowls/dishes have no where to go except laying flat face down over the tines, each taking up 1/4 to 1/3 o the lower rack. Trying to stand them up requires leaning the bowls back on tines in a 6 inch opening between the rows of tines; this positions the bowls at an angle which results in collecting dirty water. The tines are too short, too slanted and too poorly positioned to serve any useful purpose for anything other than plates and shallow pasta bowls. Plates are where this thing excels. We have relatively flat plates which fit very nicely in the lower rear rack and in the lower front rack using the adjustable tines. Very shallow pasta bowls do pretty well, too. You can fit a lot and these things always come out spotless.The upper rack for silverware gets the job done, though it takes more attention to load than a basket. If you are thoughtful about positioning items, you can load a lot of silverware and it gets cleaner than in the basket. However, my family has not yet noticed (and ignored my instructions) that the front area of the upper rack has wider spacing; they frequently put spoons there which flop over facing upwards and collect dirty water during the cycle.The bottom rack utensil basket is too shallow to hold anything that does not fit in the top rack; items just fall over into the bottom. I have only used it once or twice; it mostly just sits there empty and takes up space. However, the space is pretty useless anyway since it is just a big wide channel on the side of the rack. It smells pretty bad by the end of the day after loading dishes all day to run over night. This did not happen with our 2 previous Whirlpools. However, the filter is pretty easy to clean, though that does little to address the smell. The auto open feature is nice. Everything is dry and cool to the touch after a short drying period (except, of course, coffee mugs and things with deep rims that trap small pools of water, which is to be expected with any dishwasher).If you're into dishwasher apps on your phone, this one seems to be okay. No games or cool graphics or sounds, but lots of VERY interesting information about your dishwasher. I don't know how I ever functioned without knowing the average monthly power and water consumption for my appliance! I personally can't see the benefit of moving essential functions like delay start off the machine's control panel to a separate device, but I guess that's \'progress.\'It is very quiet, it does clean whatever you are able to get into it, and it looks nice.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher replaced my stalwart 21-year old KitchenAid.
Comments (English): [ Better than expected - even for a KitchenAid ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher replaced my stalwart 21-year old KitchenAid. So far, this one is great. LOVE the third rack, and unexpectedly so. I thought the extra rack would crowd the middle rack but it doesn't at all. Somehow the design engineers have managed to increase the space available inside this washer to add a useful, albeit skinny, third rack. Cleaning-wise, it performs better than expected - it cleans outstandingly well. Also love the large rinse agent receptacle which holds enough liquid to last a month or more. Lastly, this machine is quiet, amazingly quiet, actually. If it weren't for the status light on the door, I'd hardly be able to tell it's even running.

On the day of purchase, the installer from the partner company contacted me and sent me a photo of the installation space, and he first mentioned an additional cost of 50,000 won for the mop holder. Sentence (English): Before purchasing a dishwasher, I looked up reviews and compared product companies, and LG was the best.
Comments (English): Before purchasing a dishwasher, I looked up reviews and compared product companies, and LG was the best. The reviews were good and many people were using it, so I thought LG was the best dishwasher, and I bought it right away. Since I had to find out the size before purchasing, I contacted the call center and they gave me more accurate advice, so I was very satisfied with that. Delivery was fast at the same time as the purchase, and it arrived in just 3 days (including weekends) after purchase. Along with the installation, they kindly explained how to use it and precautions, and did a simple operation test. It was nice that the water noise was not as loud as I thought. There is a quiet mode, but it is quiet enough even in normal mode. And the cleaning power goes without saying. I put the dishes that had oil in them in the prewash and they were really clean. I really liked that the door opens slightly after the hot air drying and the air blows in at the same time, so there is not much moisture left inside after the drying process and there is no moisture inside. I wish I had bought the dishwasher a long time ago. I am 10000% satisfied.
Comments (Original): 식세기를 구입하기전에 여러 후기들을 찾아보면서 제품회사를 비교해봤는데 역시 식세기는 엘지더라구요. 후기도 좋고 정말 많은사람들이 이용하고있어서 국민식세기는 엘지구나 하고 바로 구입을했어요.참 구입전에 사이즈에 대한걸 파악해야해서 콜센터로 문의를하니 보다 정확하게 상담을 해주셔서 그것 또한 너무 만족했어요.구입과 동시에 배송이 빠르게 진행되어서 구입한지 3일(주말포함)만에 배송이 왔고, 오기전에 배송설치기사님께서 먼저 전화를 주셔서 설치 위치에 대한 사전 안내를 해드리고 설치를 해주셨어요.설치와함께 사용방법과 주의사항 같은거를 친절하게 설명해주셨고 간단하게 동작 테스트를 해주셨어요.그리고 바로 저녁에 일부러 설거지를 안해놓은 그릇들을 세척해보니 왜 국민식세기인지 알겠더라구요.먼저 육아하시는 집들은 좋은게 너무 조용해요.생각보다 물소리가 별로 안나서 좋더라구요. 조용한모드도 따로 있긴한데 일반모드로도 충분히 조용한편이에요. 그리고 세척력은 말할필요도 없어요. 기름때 있는 그릇들을 애벌세척만해서 넣었는데 정말 뽀득뽀득하게 닦여있더라구요.열풍건조후에 문이 살짝 열리면서 송풍건조를 같이해주는 시스템이라서 끝나고 내부에 습기가 차지 않고 물기가 남는게 별로 없어서 그것도 너무 맘에 들었어요. 식세기 이모님 진작 들일껄 그랬어요. 10000% 만족합니다.

Sentence (English): I love my new Maytag dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great product; terrible delivery experience ] || ---------------- || I love my new Maytag dishwasher. However, I'm giving 3 stars only because arranging for delivery and installation was an absolute nightmare. Its clear there's virtually no communication between the people who manage the Best Buy website, the Geek Squad, the off-shore customer service people, and the subcontractor providing the actual delivery and installation. Just look at this chronology:*The delivery and installation was scheduled for Tuesday, August 27th. The initial delivery window was given as 7am-7pm, with the promise of my getting a smaller 4-hour window the day before. I got no such update the day before. I kept checking the website delivery information up until 11pm the night before but had to go to sleep. When was my update expected to come, at 4 am? I had no choice but to assume they'd arrive as early as 7 am, which was annoying.*On Tuesday, the expected delivery day, an update appeared on the website by mid-morning saying the delivery window was 7am-10am. By 10:15am, no delivery. I called Geek Squad customer service. A nice guy put me on hold for 10 minutes and then told me the truck was stuck in traffic but would get to me soon.*By 4:00 pm, no delivery. I called customer service again. I was put on hold for 10-15 minutes. I was then told that the truck had broken down and there would be no delivery today. When were they going to tell me? I arranged with the representative to have the delivery and installation rescheduled for Thursday between 7am-1pm. I asked if there was anything I needed to do and was told no, that it was “taken care of”.*I checked the website on Thursday morning. To my horror, I saw that the delivery and installation had been separated into two different events. Only the “delivery” was scheduled; I needed to schedule the “installation”. This made no sense because obviously the team that delivers the appliance always installs it. The online system indicated there were no “installation” appointments available for two weeks. Again, I called customer service. They said there was nothing they could do, that I needed to schedule the installation, and that I might not even get delivery of the item today. Huh? But here's the punchline: the moment I ended the call the delivery team arrived. They delivered and installed the dishwasher.*I want to give a shout-out to the delivery and installation contractor, Starling Logistics. The lead technician, Frank, and his assistant were friendly, efficient, and effective. The dishwasher was installed perfectly.In sum, there was virtually no coordination between the entities responsible getting the appliance to my home and installed. I was left stuck at home, waiting endlessly with no updates until I called (and don't think its easy to figure out what number to call.) Shame on Best Buy. Whoever's responsible for Best Buy delivery and installation operations better get their act together. Given this experience, I will not be purchasing an appliance from Best Buy again.

Sentence (English): It is a good dishwasher, and I bought it because it is a two drawer dishwasher.
Comments (English): It is a good dishwasher, and I bought it because it is a two drawer dishwasher. Maybe not quite as good as the Fisher- Paykel I had for 15 years. The racks are super good and sturdy, well thought out. Not pleased that I cannot use liquid dishwasher detergent in this Cafe. And the pods have to be placed somewhere else in the dishwasher, other than in the pod container provided. The starting of the dishwasher is okay, not great, slightly a problem. Also, that there is no way to tell, like a light and timer on the outside of the door, how long the dishwasher has been going and time left. The really weird thing is that to open the dishwasher drawers you hav to knock on the outside of the drawer 3 times. And, we found out just recently, if the power is out the drawers will not open. Love having the two drawers though, so much more convenient. Have been using this Cafe dishwasher for two weeks, it does get the dishes clean.

Sentence (English): We purchased this dishwasher through Inside Pass and it was delivered on October 18, 2022.
Comments (English): [ Under two years old and it's toast - My Experience ] || ---------------- || We purchased this dishwasher through Inside Pass and it was delivered on October 18, 2022. This is less than two years ago, and we have been diligent about caring for our dishwasher. Less than two years old and it's dead. DEAD - will not turn on - not a flicker of light from this thing. This is after a long and excruciating process with the customer service department. Buyer beware; it's pretty and if you can afford to replace an expensive appliance every 1.5-2 years, do your thing. I've included the details of my experience below. To kick things off - installation was paid for as well as the installation hose equipment. The installer told me that I did not need the installation equipment as I had paid the installation charge. The installer took the install package and told me that they would refund this purchase. Even after multiple communications, hours of wait time, I never got a refund. Shortly after the installation, we noticed that the dishwasher wasn't secured nor was it leveled by the installer. I contacted customer service multiple times and I was told to troubleshoot it myself and essentially uninstall the dishwasher that I paid to have installed, fix it, and install it correctly. This is unacceptable; however, we did fix it as we didn't want our new dishwasher to break while we were trying to finagle the door shut to run the dishwasher. The installation was done so terribly that we had to push down on the right side of the dishwasher in order for the door to close under our countertop. It usually worked unless the WHOLE ENTIRE dishwasher pushed back into the cabinet space - at that point I would pull it back out, push down on the right side, and push the door closed while holding the bottom in place with my toe so it wouldn't slide back again. We're nothing if not innovative. :/ Alrighty - this brings me to the main event. This weekend we had our dishwasher loaded and ready to rocky (door closed and everything). I noticed that something was leaking out of the bottom left corner of the dishwasher. I cleaned it up and went on with the process to run the dishwaher. Just kidding. F6E1 started flashing on the control panel. We broke out the Google box, YouTube, owner's manual, Reddit, etc. We followed the user manual that correlated with what we were seeing online. We eventually shut the power off to the unit for a couple minutes. Upon turning the power back on, it was flashing 1 instead of F6E1. Progress? Nope. We shut the power off again, waited a bit, and now NOTTA, ZIP, ZILCH. No Lights - not even a flicker. I tried contacting customer service - it was a holiday. No problem, everyone needs a holiday weekend. Today, I tried contacting them through the Whirlpool website and the Inside Pass site. I'm still waiting for Inside Pass; I've waited through my entire lunch hour in addition to the 30 minutes I've taken to write the review. I waited for 20 minutes for the Whirlpool chat - upon which, I didn't respond within 30 seconds and the chat was ended. At that point, I logged on and started penning this review. This experience has been incredibly disappointing and after a year and a half of paying for fertility treatments out of pocket- we don't have hundreds of dollars to bring out a repair man (anticipated charge on WP website). Nor do I have the funds to order a new dishwasher. Not sure what I do from here because I can't get a hold of anyone that will support me. Do I scrap it? Start GoFundMe? Kidding aside - I hope that not a single person has this same experience. I have felt disposable, disregarded, and disrespected through this experience. Whirlpool, please do better and be better. Your customers deserve better products, service, and support.

Description led one to think there was a third silverware rack for the top as in the other models, instead there are two poorly designed silverware caddies which take up a lot of space in the lower rack and fit little silverware. Our old Maytag was much better designed and held much more in the way of dishes and silverware. In addition, when you roll out the bottom rack, there is a gap between the track on the door and the track on the machine, the rack essentially falls into this gap every time you pull the bottom rack out. The old Maytag had the same gap, but it was shorter and once loaded, the rack wheels were situated such that the gap between them didn’t allow the rack to fall into the gap.The door is very resistant to opening. This unit was designed for a customizable front. This problem occurred before the cover panel was added. Operates fine with the cover panel but opening requires significant pulling- as if the spring is too tight or oversized. Better than undersized I guess, but really needs to be pulled in order to open.I would say the primary good features are that it is quiet and it seems to clean well, but design wise, very disappointing.I don’t know if these issues are for Home Depot or Bosch, but Home Depot asked us to rate the appliance. Based on the issues we are having with the poor capacity and door design, I would give it a 3 so far.

Sentence (English): The 10 year old dishwasher that I replaced worked fantastic with straightforward controls on the unit.
Comments (English): [ Technology gone amuck ] || ---------------- || The 10 year old dishwasher that I replaced worked fantastic with straightforward controls on the unit. It always got the dishes clean and mostly dry as well. When it needed replacing I decided to go with Bosch. BIG mistake. 1. The Short Cycle on my previous machine could be run with a drying option. Not the Bosch. Speed 60 can't be run with a drying option. 2. The Rinse Cycle, Delicate Cycle and Eco Options aren't available on the machine, only on the App, a BIG disadvantage. The highly touted "Crystal Dry" honestly does no better than my previous machine's "Heated Dry" and using Sanitize and extended dry options actually dries just as well as Crystal Dry. But the biggest problem I have, for the 7 months I've owned this dishwasher, is the unit doesn't work correctly. As the photo shows, I selected the Heavy Cycle with Crystal Dry and Santize options and a "Custom" power setting for the power arm (only available through the App) and the total running time is going to be 1 minute! I pressed the start button and sure enough, it started running for 1 minute. In addition, sometimes I will set a cycle, (eg. Normal with Crystral Dry) which should take around 2 1/2 hours and the dishwasher runs for over 4 hours! When I see what the "Last Selected" was it sometimes has the correct cycle and sometimes has some random cycle selected. Bosch has come out to examine the machine several times and each time claims it is operating normally. There is also the occasional E-31 error which cause my floor to get flooded despite the fact that Aqua Stop is supposed to avoid that. It obviously doesn't. The tech's solution is to not use Pods which he said is not supposed to be used in Bosch dishwashers, despite the fact that they come with a complementary package of Finish Quantum. Sometimes the dishes come out clean and reasonably dry. Sometimes they come out dirty and wet with the same cycle and options selected. Again, Bosch says it's operating normally. Well, if this is normal then I'd never buy a Bosch again. Oh how I wish I had purchased the same brand that I had for 10 years and 10 years before that. There are 3 settings for the sensor, 4 adjustable zones, 10 levels for the rinse aid, 4 levels for notification and button sound levels, and three "remote start options" for the App, "Monitoring" where you can see what the dishwasher is doing but not make any changes, permanent remote, where the App can start and stop the dishwasher, and "Manual Remote" in which you can set it up with the App but you have to push the button on the dishwasher itself to start it. When and Why anyone would ever need to use "Manual Remote" is beyond my comprehension. This thing is a nightmare of technology that doesn't even work correctly. Oh, it also needs a Junction Box installed for it to plug into instead of just plugging in the way the previous unit did. I'm sorry I ever bought this expensive headache.

Sentence (English): Preamble to Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect It's been 4 weeks since I provided my appliance dealer with detailed written feedback about my new Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Frustrating User Interface ] || ---------------- || Preamble to Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect It's been 4 weeks since I provided my appliance dealer with detailed written feedback about my new Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher. My dealer promptly forwarded my written feedback to his Bosch rep, who forwarded it to the appropriate Bosch | Home Connect development team. My written feedback contained detailed descriptions of my specific concerns and complaints, which are discussed below. After 4 weeks … “crickets” … i.e., no response from Bosch. I called Bosch's customer service (***-***-****) once in my early days of ownership, but was dissatisfied with their support. (For example, the customer service rep told me that I could tell when the dishwasher had completing cleaning the dishes because the front display would show “00:00”. I tried to explain that the display went dark after a few minutes. IOW, it's dark the next morning when I go downstairs to the kitchen). I quickly became frustrated with my conversation with Bosch customer service, and said “Thanks” and hung up. As a result of my experience, I'm disinclined to talk with a Bosch customer service rep again. If someone from Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect product management (or a manager for the relevant software development team) wants to talk and/or email with me, I'm open to a professional and respectful conversation, and I'm open to providing feedback for any Beta software that addresses my complaints. Bottom line: Bosch had ample opportunity to address my concerns before I posted the following review. I'll appreciate hearing constructive feedback from other owners of the Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N. Robert ----------------------------------------------------- Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect I prefer to have my dishwasher run after midnight so that heat and moisture isn't pumped into my kitchen on a hot summer day, and so that I'd not annoyed by noise during waking hours, and to take advantage of off-peak electrical power. This dishwasher is usually quiet, except that it's louder than any dishwasher I've owned – by far - when it's discharging water. Even though the dishwasher is downstairs, I've been roused from sleep by the sound of the dishwasher discharging water. Every other dishwasher I've owned enabled me to quickly and easily delay the start, without having to read an instruction manual, or download software to a smartphone. However, this BOSCH Benchmark dishwasher does not have a physical button (i.e., on the front of the appliance) dedicated to delaying the dishwasher's start. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Installation of the Home Connect smartphone app is not straightforward. (Even though I scanned the QR code on the dishwasher as part of the installation of the Home Connect smartphone app, the installation instructions weren't specific to the Bosch Benchmark dishwasher, and were therefore confusing.) The user interface (“UI”) for the Home Connect smartphone app is not easy to learn, because of the app's complexity, and because of very poorly written documentation. (I've read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.) It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work. There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident. (Here's just one arcane example: Buried in the app's Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance's front panel.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) On another occasion when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher's panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn't work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. Finally I was able to activate “delay start”. It is NOT AT ALL self-evident how to use this dishwasher's complicated and cumbersome user interface – at least when using the “delay start” feature. As part of Bosch's product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? It certainly doesn't appear so. A dishwasher shouldn't be this difficult to operate. No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation. The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren't the only problems. The Bosch Benchmark dishwasher does not have an indicator or display (i.e., on the front of the appliance) that shows that the dishwasher has completed its cycles, and the dishes are clean, and the dishwasher is ready to be unloaded. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher's front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? If support for the Home Connect app is discontinued, will I be stuck with a dishwasher that has limited functionality? Another problem: The inside of the dishwasher is always wet, even after activating every option that (according to the documentation) is supposed to minimize the wetness. This causes me to be concerned about sanitation inside the dishwasher, in spite of the fact that the “Use and Care Manual” says it is normal for the inside of the dishwasher to be wet. I always run “Sanitize” (documentation states ”continuous use of this option improves the hygiene status”) and “Crystal Dry” modes, and I've activated the setting for “Intensive Dry” (which is buried in a “Settings” menu). And I use a rinse aid. (Bosch touts the Zeolith drying as an energy saving feature.) These settings that are required to sanitize the dishwasher and get the dishes dry result in a cycle time of 3 hours and 10 minutes. I've never owned a dishwasher that took anywhere near this long to wash and dry the dishes. This is another reason I want to use “delay start” and have the dishwasher run in the wee hours. (FYI: There is a “Speed 60®” option, however sanitization and drying apparently are compromised.) IMO, this dishwasher's design (particularly its user interface) is unacceptably bad. What causes Bosch to think that consumers would want to spend this amount of time – and endure this amount of aggravation – just to run a dishwasher? I point out that the Bosch Benchmark™ is an expensive dishwasher. IMO a premium appliance should make the owner's life easier, not more complicated. I've never had the displeasure of owning a dishwasher that required the investment of so many hours to learn to operate it. P.S. I've rated two stars instead of one because the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher cleans my dishes. (With that said, I do VERY little cooking. Therefore, someone else who gets lots of pot and pans REALLY dirty will be better equipped to discuss this dishwasher's ability to clean.)

This dishwasher is usually quiet, except that it's louder than any dishwasher I've owned – by far - when it's discharging water. Even though the dishwasher is downstairs, I've been roused from sleep by the sound of the dishwasher discharging water. Every other dishwasher I've owned enabled me to quickly and easily delay the start, without having to read an instruction manual, or download software to a smartphone. However, this BOSCH Benchmark dishwasher does not have a physical button (i.e., on the front of the appliance) dedicated to delaying the dishwasher's start. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Installation of the Home Connect smartphone app is not straightforward. (Even though I scanned the QR code on the dishwasher as part of the installation of the Home Connect smartphone app, the installation instructions weren't specific to the Bosch Benchmark dishwasher, and were therefore confusing.) The user interface (“UI”) for the Home Connect smartphone app is not easy to learn, because of the app's complexity, and because of very poorly written documentation. (I've read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.) It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work. There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident. (Here's just one arcane example: Buried in the app's Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance's front panel.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) On another occasion when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher's panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn't work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. Finally I was able to activate “delay start”. It is NOT AT ALL self-evident how to use this dishwasher's complicated and cumbersome user interface – at least when using the “delay start” feature. As part of Bosch's product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? It certainly doesn't appear so. A dishwasher shouldn't be this difficult to operate. No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation. The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren't the only problems. The Bosch Benchmark dishwasher does not have an indicator or display (i.e., on the front of the appliance) that shows that the dishwasher has completed its cycles, and the dishes are clean, and the dishwasher is ready to be unloaded. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher's front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? If support for the Home Connect app is discontinued, will I be stuck with a dishwasher that has limited functionality? And I use a rinse aid. (Bosch touts the Zeolith drying as an energy saving feature.) These settings that are required to sanitize the dishwasher and get the dishes dry result in a cycle time of 3 hours and 10 minutes. (FYI: There is a “Speed 60®” option, however sanitization and drying apparently are compromised.) IMO, this dishwasher's design (particularly its user interface) is unacceptably bad. What causes Bosch to think that consumers would want to spend this amount of time – and endure this amount of aggravation – just to run a dishwasher? Robert ----------------------------------------------------- Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect I prefer to have my dishwasher run after midnight so that heat and moisture isn't pumped into my kitchen on a hot summer day, and so that I'd not annoyed by noise during waking hours, and to take advantage of off-peak electrical power. This dishwasher is usually quiet, except that it's louder than any dishwasher I've owned – by far - when it's discharging water. Even though the dishwasher is downstairs, I've been roused from sleep by the sound of the dishwasher discharging water. Every other dishwasher I've owned enabled me to quickly and easily delay the start, without having to read an instruction manual, or download software to a smartphone. However, this BOSCH Benchmark dishwasher does not have a physical button (i.e., on the front of the appliance) dedicated to delaying the dishwasher's start. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Installation of the Home Connect smartphone app is not straightforward. (Even though I scanned the QR code on the dishwasher as part of the installation of the Home Connect smartphone app, the installation instructions weren't specific to the Bosch Benchmark dishwasher, and were therefore confusing.) The user interface (“UI”) for the Home Connect smartphone app is not easy to learn, because of the app's complexity, and because of very poorly written documentation. (I've read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.) It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work. There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident. (Here's just one arcane example: Buried in the app's Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance's front panel.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) On another occasion when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher's panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn't work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. Finally I was able to activate “delay start”. It is NOT AT ALL self-evident how to use this dishwasher's complicated and cumbersome user interface – at least when using the “delay start” feature. As part of Bosch's product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? It certainly doesn't appear so. A dishwasher shouldn't be this difficult to operate. No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation. The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren't the only problems. The Bosch Benchmark dishwasher does not have an indicator or display (i.e., on the front of the appliance) that shows that the dishwasher has completed its cycles, and the dishes are clean, and the dishwasher is ready to be unloaded. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher's front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? If support for the Home Connect app is discontinued, will I be stuck with a dishwasher that has limited functionality? Another problem: The inside of the dishwasher is always wet, even after activating every option that (according to the documentation) is supposed to minimize the wetness. This causes me to be concerned about sanitation inside the dishwasher, in spite of the fact that the “Use and Care Manual” says it is normal for the inside of the dishwasher to be wet. I always run “Sanitize” (documentation states ”continuous use of this option improves the hygiene status”) and “Crystal Dry” modes, and I've activated the setting for “Intensive Dry” (which is buried in a “Settings” menu). And I use a rinse aid. (Bosch touts the Zeolith drying as an energy saving feature.) These settings that are required to sanitize the dishwasher and get the dishes dry result in a cycle time of 3 hours and 10 minutes. I've never owned a dishwasher that took anywhere near this long to wash and dry the dishes. This is another reason I want to use “delay start” and have the dishwasher run in the wee hours. (FYI: There is a “Speed 60®” option, however sanitization and drying apparently are compromised.) IMO, this dishwasher's design (particularly its user interface) is unacceptably bad. What causes Bosch to think that consumers would want to spend this amount of time – and endure this amount of aggravation – just to run a dishwasher? I point out that the Bosch Benchmark™ is an expensive dishwasher. IMO a premium appliance should make the owner's life easier, not more complicated. I've never had the displeasure of owning a dishwasher that required the investment of so many hours to learn to operate it. P.S. I've rated two stars instead of one because the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher cleans my dishes. (With that said, I do VERY little cooking. Therefore, someone else who gets lots of pot and pans REALLY dirty will be better equipped to discuss this dishwasher's ability to clean.)
