Robert ----------------------------------------------------- Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect I prefer to have my dishwasher run after midnight so that heat and moisture isn't pumped into my kitchen on a hot summer day, and so that I'd not annoyed by noise during waking hours, and to take advantage of off-peak electrical power. This dishwasher is usually quiet, except that it's louder than any dishwasher I've owned – by far - when it's discharging water. Even though the dishwasher is downstairs, I've been roused from sleep by the sound of the dishwasher discharging water. Every other dishwasher I've owned enabled me to quickly and easily delay the start, without having to read an instruction manual, or download software to a smartphone. However, this BOSCH Benchmark dishwasher does not have a physical button (i.e., on the front of the appliance) dedicated to delaying the dishwasher's start. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Installation of the Home Connect smartphone app is not straightforward. (Even though I scanned the QR code on the dishwasher as part of the installation of the Home Connect smartphone app, the installation instructions weren't specific to the Bosch Benchmark dishwasher, and were therefore confusing.) The user interface (“UI”) for the Home Connect smartphone app is not easy to learn, because of the app's complexity, and because of very poorly written documentation. (I've read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.) It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work. There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident. (Here's just one arcane example: Buried in the app's Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance's front panel.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) On another occasion when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher's panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn't work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. Finally I was able to activate “delay start”. It is NOT AT ALL self-evident how to use this dishwasher's complicated and cumbersome user interface – at least when using the “delay start” feature. As part of Bosch's product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? It certainly doesn't appear so. A dishwasher shouldn't be this difficult to operate. No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation. The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren't the only problems. The Bosch Benchmark dishwasher does not have an indicator or display (i.e., on the front of the appliance) that shows that the dishwasher has completed its cycles, and the dishes are clean, and the dishwasher is ready to be unloaded. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher's front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? If support for the Home Connect app is discontinued, will I be stuck with a dishwasher that has limited functionality? Another problem: The inside of the dishwasher is always wet, even after activating every option that (according to the documentation) is supposed to minimize the wetness. This causes me to be concerned about sanitation inside the dishwasher, in spite of the fact that the “Use and Care Manual” says it is normal for the inside of the dishwasher to be wet. I always run “Sanitize” (documentation states ”continuous use of this option improves the hygiene status”) and “Crystal Dry” modes, and I've activated the setting for “Intensive Dry” (which is buried in a “Settings” menu). And I use a rinse aid. (Bosch touts the Zeolith drying as an energy saving feature.) These settings that are required to sanitize the dishwasher and get the dishes dry result in a cycle time of 3 hours and 10 minutes. I've never owned a dishwasher that took anywhere near this long to wash and dry the dishes. This is another reason I want to use “delay start” and have the dishwasher run in the wee hours. (FYI: There is a “Speed 60®” option, however sanitization and drying apparently are compromised.) IMO, this dishwasher's design (particularly its user interface) is unacceptably bad. What causes Bosch to think that consumers would want to spend this amount of time – and endure this amount of aggravation – just to run a dishwasher? I point out that the Bosch Benchmark™ is an expensive dishwasher. IMO a premium appliance should make the owner's life easier, not more complicated. I've never had the displeasure of owning a dishwasher that required the investment of so many hours to learn to operate it. P.S. I've rated two stars instead of one because the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher cleans my dishes. (With that said, I do VERY little cooking. Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. Robert ----------------------------------------------------- Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect I prefer to have my dishwasher run after midnight so that heat and moisture isn't pumped into my kitchen on a hot summer day, and so that I'd not annoyed by noise during waking hours, and to take advantage of off-peak electrical power. This dishwasher is usually quiet, except that it's louder than any dishwasher I've owned – by far - when it's discharging water. Even though the dishwasher is downstairs, I've been roused from sleep by the sound of the dishwasher discharging water. Every other dishwasher I've owned enabled me to quickly and easily delay the start, without having to read an instruction manual, or download software to a smartphone. However, this BOSCH Benchmark dishwasher does not have a physical button (i.e., on the front of the appliance) dedicated to delaying the dishwasher's start. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Installation of the Home Connect smartphone app is not straightforward. (Even though I scanned the QR code on the dishwasher as part of the installation of the Home Connect smartphone app, the installation instructions weren't specific to the Bosch Benchmark dishwasher, and were therefore confusing.) The user interface (“UI”) for the Home Connect smartphone app is not easy to learn, because of the app's complexity, and because of very poorly written documentation. (I've read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.) It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work. There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident. (Here's just one arcane example: Buried in the app's Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance's front panel.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) On another occasion when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher's panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn't work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. Finally I was able to activate “delay start”. It is NOT AT ALL self-evident how to use this dishwasher's complicated and cumbersome user interface – at least when using the “delay start” feature. As part of Bosch's product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? It certainly doesn't appear so. A dishwasher shouldn't be this difficult to operate. No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation. The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren't the only problems. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher's front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? Another problem: The inside of the dishwasher is always wet, even after activating every option that (according to the documentation) is supposed to minimize the wetness. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) (I’ve read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.)It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work.  There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident.  (Here’s just one arcane example: Buried in the app’s Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance’s front panel.)Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect’s “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies.Once when I couldn’t get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn’t tell you this.)On another occasion when I couldn’t get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher’s panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”)After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn’t get delay start to work.  I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn’t work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. As part of Bosch’s product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation.The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren’t the only problems.The Bosch Benchmark dishwasher does not have an indicator or display (i.e., on the front of the appliance) that shows that the dishwasher has completed its cycles, and the dishes are clean, and the dishwasher is ready to be unloaded. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher’s front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn’t a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation?IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn’t identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …)$64k Question:  What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported?  What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? If support for the Home Connect app is discontinued, will I be stuck with a dishwasher that has limited functionality?Another problem:  The inside of the dishwasher is always wet, even after activating every option that (according to the documentation) is supposed to minimize the wetness. This causes me to be concerned about sanitation inside the dishwasher, in spite of the fact that the “Use and Care Manual” says it is normal for the inside of the dishwasher to be wet. I always run “Sanitize” (documentation states ”continuous use of this option improves the hygiene status”) and “Crystal Dry” modes, and I’ve activated the setting for “Intensive Dry” (which is buried in a “Settings” menu). And I use a rinse aid. (Bosch touts the Zeolith drying as an energy saving feature.) These settings that are required to sanitize the dishwasher and get the dishes dry result in a cycle time of 3 hours and 10 minutes. I’ve never owned a dishwasher that took anywhere near this long to wash and dry the dishes. This is another reason I want to use “delay start” and have the dishwasher run in the wee hours. (FYI:  There is a “Speed 60®” option, however sanitization and drying apparently are compromised.)IMO, this dishwasher’s design (particularly its user interface) is unacceptably bad. What causes Bosch to think that consumers would want to spend this amount of time – and endure this amount of aggravation – just to run a dishwasher? I point out that the Bosch Benchmark™ is an expensive dishwasher. IMO a premium appliance should make the owner’s life easier, not more complicated. I’ve never had the displeasure of owning a dishwasher that required the investment of so many hours to learn to operate it. P.S.  I’ve rated two stars instead of one because the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher cleans my dishes. (With that said, I do VERY little cooking. Robert ----------------------------------------------------- Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect I prefer to have my dishwasher run after midnight so that heat and moisture isn't pumped into my kitchen on a hot summer day, and so that I'd not annoyed by noise during waking hours, and to take advantage of off-peak electrical power. This dishwasher is usually quiet, except that it's louder than any dishwasher I've owned – by far - when it's discharging water. Even though the dishwasher is downstairs, I've been roused from sleep by the sound of the dishwasher discharging water. Every other dishwasher I've owned enabled me to quickly and easily delay the start, without having to read an instruction manual, or download software to a smartphone. However, this BOSCH Benchmark dishwasher does not have a physical button (i.e., on the front of the appliance) dedicated to delaying the dishwasher's start. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Installation of the Home Connect smartphone app is not straightforward. (Even though I scanned the QR code on the dishwasher as part of the installation of the Home Connect smartphone app, the installation instructions weren't specific to the Bosch Benchmark dishwasher, and were therefore confusing.) The user interface (“UI”) for the Home Connect smartphone app is not easy to learn, because of the app's complexity, and because of very poorly written documentation. (I've read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.) It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work. There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident. (Here's just one arcane example: Buried in the app's Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance's front panel.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) On another occasion when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher's panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn't work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. Finally I was able to activate “delay start”. It is NOT AT ALL self-evident how to use this dishwasher's complicated and cumbersome user interface – at least when using the “delay start” feature. As part of Bosch's product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? It certainly doesn't appear so. A dishwasher shouldn't be this difficult to operate. No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation. The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren't the only problems. The Bosch Benchmark dishwasher does not have an indicator or display (i.e., on the front of the appliance) that shows that the dishwasher has completed its cycles, and the dishes are clean, and the dishwasher is ready to be unloaded. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher's front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? If support for the Home Connect app is discontinued, will I be stuck with a dishwasher that has limited functionality? Another problem: The inside of the dishwasher is always wet, even after activating every option that (according to the documentation) is supposed to minimize the wetness. This causes me to be concerned about sanitation inside the dishwasher, in spite of the fact that the “Use and Care Manual” says it is normal for the inside of the dishwasher to be wet. I always run “Sanitize” (documentation states ”continuous use of this option improves the hygiene status”) and “Crystal Dry” modes, and I've activated the setting for “Intensive Dry” (which is buried in a “Settings” menu). And I use a rinse aid. (Bosch touts the Zeolith drying as an energy saving feature.) These settings that are required to sanitize the dishwasher and get the dishes dry result in a cycle time of 3 hours and 10 minutes. I've never owned a dishwasher that took anywhere near this long to wash and dry the dishes. This is another reason I want to use “delay start” and have the dishwasher run in the wee hours. (FYI: There is a “Speed 60®” option, however sanitization and drying apparently are compromised.) IMO, this dishwasher's design (particularly its user interface) is unacceptably bad. What causes Bosch to think that consumers would want to spend this amount of time – and endure this amount of aggravation – just to run a dishwasher? I point out that the Bosch Benchmark™ is an expensive dishwasher. IMO a premium appliance should make the owner's life easier, not more complicated. I've never had the displeasure of owning a dishwasher that required the investment of so many hours to learn to operate it. P.S. I've rated two stars instead of one because the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher cleans my dishes. (With that said, I do VERY little cooking. Therefore, someone else who gets lots of pot and pans REALLY dirty will be better equipped to discuss this dishwasher's ability to clean.)

Robert ----------------------------------------------------- Review of Bosch Benchmark™ Series Dishwasher SHP9PCM5N | Home Connect I prefer to have my dishwasher run after midnight so that heat and moisture isn't pumped into my kitchen on a hot summer day, and so that I'd not annoyed by noise during waking hours, and to take advantage of off-peak electrical power. This dishwasher is usually quiet, except that it's louder than any dishwasher I've owned – by far - when it's discharging water. Even though the dishwasher is downstairs, I've been roused from sleep by the sound of the dishwasher discharging water. Every other dishwasher I've owned enabled me to quickly and easily delay the start, without having to read an instruction manual, or download software to a smartphone. However, this BOSCH Benchmark dishwasher does not have a physical button (i.e., on the front of the appliance) dedicated to delaying the dishwasher's start. Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Installation of the Home Connect smartphone app is not straightforward. (Even though I scanned the QR code on the dishwasher as part of the installation of the Home Connect smartphone app, the installation instructions weren't specific to the Bosch Benchmark dishwasher, and were therefore confusing.) The user interface (“UI”) for the Home Connect smartphone app is not easy to learn, because of the app's complexity, and because of very poorly written documentation. (I've read all of the Bosch Benchmark™ | Home Connect documentation that I can find.) It took me many hours of trial-and-error to get the “delay start” feature to work. There are many options that must be set, and steps to execute – many of which are NOT self-evident. (Here's just one arcane example: Buried in the app's Settings, “Remote Control Level” must be set to “Permanent”, and IIRC this requires a confirmation action by pushing a button on the appliance's front panel.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) On another occasion when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, again it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., I had opened the dishwasher door to add a dish, and apparently the “delay start” is cancelled until the START button on the dishwasher's panel is pressed. (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) That didn't work - after two tries. I then unplugged the dishwasher, and waited for several minutes for the dishwasher to go through its boot-up process. Finally I was able to activate “delay start”. It is NOT AT ALL self-evident how to use this dishwasher's complicated and cumbersome user interface – at least when using the “delay start” feature. As part of Bosch's product development, did Bosch conduct user acceptance testing (“UAT”) wherein average consumers unfamiliar with the product are tasked to install and use the app without training or assistance? It certainly doesn't appear so. A dishwasher shouldn't be this difficult to operate. No customer should have to endure this level of aggravation. The “delay start” feature and the Home Connect app aren't the only problems. The Bosch Benchmark dishwasher does not have an indicator or display (i.e., on the front of the appliance) that shows that the dishwasher has completed its cycles, and the dishes are clean, and the dishwasher is ready to be unloaded. (After running, the front panel of the appliance goes completely dark after a few minutes – i.e., the dishwasher's front panel display appears the same as if it had NOT run.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. IOW, there is no way to know that the dishwasher actually ran and the dishes are clean, without accessing the smartphone app. IMO this is ridiculously inconvenient. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? If support for the Home Connect app is discontinued, will I be stuck with a dishwasher that has limited functionality? Another problem: The inside of the dishwasher is always wet, even after activating every option that (according to the documentation) is supposed to minimize the wetness. This causes me to be concerned about sanitation inside the dishwasher, in spite of the fact that the “Use and Care Manual” says it is normal for the inside of the dishwasher to be wet. I always run “Sanitize” (documentation states ”continuous use of this option improves the hygiene status”) and “Crystal Dry” modes, and I've activated the setting for “Intensive Dry” (which is buried in a “Settings” menu). And I use a rinse aid. (Bosch touts the Zeolith drying as an energy saving feature.) These settings that are required to sanitize the dishwasher and get the dishes dry result in a cycle time of 3 hours and 10 minutes. I've never owned a dishwasher that took anywhere near this long to wash and dry the dishes. This is another reason I want to use “delay start” and have the dishwasher run in the wee hours. (FYI: There is a “Speed 60®” option, however sanitization and drying apparently are compromised.) IMO, this dishwasher's design (particularly its user interface) is unacceptably bad. What causes Bosch to think that consumers would want to spend this amount of time – and endure this amount of aggravation – just to run a dishwasher? Bosch implements the “delay start” feature via a smartphone app called Home Connect. (Home Connect does not offer a PC browser interface.) Even after investing many hours to get the Home Connect's “delay start” feature to work, over the next several weeks I encountered several frustrating operational/UI anomalies. Once when I couldn't get “delay start” to work, it took me an inordinate amount of time to discover the problem – i.e., the dishwasher was ON, and apparently it must be OFF to activate delay start. (The app doesn't tell you this.) (The “Use and Care Manual” contains the following statement “Your dishwasher has a built in feature to help prevent unintentional operation, e.g. by children. After starting the appliance, the door has to be closed within 4 seconds, otherwise the operation will be paused.”) After several weeks of ownership, I thought I had learned all of the operational oddities. However – once again – one evening I couldn't get delay start to work. I had to carry my smartphone downstairs and stand in front of the dishwasher for 20 minutes trying everything I could think of. I reset the dishwasher by pressing the POWER button for 4 seconds. (This is confusing because the reboot requires several minutes of inscrutable steps for the dishwasher to execute.) Bosch implements a status feature buried in the Home Connect smartphone app, however this smart-phone based app is very inconvenient compared with a display on the appliance. This feature deficiency would be particularly problematic in a home with multiple users, where it would be easy for someone to unknowingly load dirty dishes into a dishwasher that contains dishes that have been cleaned. Why doesn't a top-of-the-line dishwasher have front panel displays that are essential for its operation? IMO, the use of a smartphone app should be optional for a home appliance, not required in order to use basic features such as “delay start”. BTW, if a user chooses not to use the Home Connect app with the Bosch Benchmark™ dishwasher, apparently they must press “Button A” (which isn't identified on the appliance) to access software options via an arcane user interface. (Good luck with that …) $64k Question: What happens when the Home Connect app is no longer supported? What assurance does Bosch provide that the Home Connect app will be supported for the next 15 - 20 years? Sentence (English): We bought a WDP540HAMZ Whirlpool dishwasher to replace a Whirlpool we had for 10 years.
Comments (English): [ The good, the bad and the not so good. ] || ---------------- || We bought a WDP540HAMZ Whirlpool dishwasher to replace a Whirlpool we had for 10 years. We got a great price in store so that we only paid $100 more over the one we purchased 10 years earlier. As with all government regulated technology you take one step forward and two steps backward. We do save water with the new machine but a cycle takes much longer (a loss of time) which then uses more electricity (a loss of energy). The heating/drying options work very poorly so that we have to dry many of the dishes, especially plastic, which our previous dishwasher did a decent job of drying. That's a 3rd step backward. We rinse our dishes well before washing so that we use the machine more for disinfecting than cleaning (the cleaning seems to be a stronger feature of the machine). We purchased a 5 year warranty because we don't trust modern technology. While we were disappointed that they no longer put the silverware utensil rack on the door they have widened it and put it on the bottom rack inside which enables us to put all our utensils-even ladles-in it rather than lay them sideways on the racks. We love this but dislike the lose of space for dishes in the lower rack. We like the fact that the machine remembers the previous setting we used for washing, that the buttons are on the top of the door instead of on the front and that the door is stainless steel inside and out so that it feels more heavy duty and looks good. I've found that for some reason on a few occasions a particular plastic plate will be left with a soap film on it while those around it are fine. It is a little noisier than our previous dishwasher but not objectionably so. If this thing lasts for another 10 years I would probably raise my rating from a 3 to a 4.

Sentence (English): I bought the latest product, but it doesn't seem to clean as well as I expected.
Comments (English): I bought the latest product, but it doesn't seem to clean as well as I expected. I'm thinking about whether I should use the steam function every time. The knife holder newly included in the 24-year model doesn't clean the outside of the knife, and it's not very useful. I use it separately to secure the maximum internal space. When I looked at it in the store, the interior was dark gray, including the accessories. It looked stylish, but when I actually used it, there was a disadvantage that the color was dark and hard to see when food scraps, etc. were stuck on the inside or when they got dirty. The internal accessories (trays, rollers, etc.) of the German-made dishwasher I used for 20 years were white, so I think the difference is more obvious. Since personal preferences vary, I hope that bright-colored accessories will come out so that I can change them when I need to.
Comments (Original): 최신 제품을 샀는데, 기대만큼 깨끗한 세척은 안되는것 같습니다. 매번 스팀 기능을 써야하는건지 생각 중입니다. 24년형에 새로 포함된 칼꽂이는 칼 바깥쪽 세척이 안되고, 효용성이 떨어져, 최대한의 내부 공간 확보 위해 분리해놓고 사용하고 있어요. 매장에서 볼때는 내부가 악세서리 포함, 진회색 인것이, 세련되어 보였는데 막상 사용하면서 보니, 내부에 음식물 찌꺼기 등이 붙어있거나, 때가 끼었을 때, 색상이 어두워 눈에 잘 띄지 않는 단점도 있습니다. 이전에  20년간 썼던 독일제 식세기 내부 악세서리(트레이, 롤러 등) 가 흰색이었어서 더 차이가 뚜렸이 보이는것 같아요. 개인의 기호가 있으니,  밝은색 악세서리도 나와서, 교체 필요시, 바꿔볼수 있기를 기대해 봅니다.

Sentence (English): This unit replace an 11 year old GE Profile.
Comments (English): [ So far so good. ] || ---------------- || This unit replace an 11 year old GE Profile. Install was relatively easy, though the connections are in the back and the GE's were in the front. There is a plug instead of a two or three wire pigtail so you'll need to have an outlet installed. The unit cleans well. I would say that loading can be haphazard and it will still clean all of the dishes. This wasn't my expierence with the GE. The top controls aren't that intuituve. To get the most out of the unit you'll need to use the app. I still can't start the wash from the control panel wihtout at least two tries. There is a red light that shines on the floor to let you know the wash is in progress. If it's blinking, it's paused. One thing I've noticed is that with a manual filter you have to clean it after each use. Otherwise the inside will smell after a couple days. There are just two of us so we usually wait a week until we run a full load. Doing that with this unit emits an all out rotting odor. We've found the rinse feature does help a little. Cleaning the filter is relatively easy and takes about 3 minutes. We usually run the unit after dinner, have it set to automatically open the door when finished. I'll pull the drawers out and let it finish drying over night. By the next morning the dishes are all completely dry. I'd buy this unit again despite the reliance on the app. It cleans well which is the main reason. It can just be a little difficlut to get there.

There are just two of us so we usually wait a week until we run a full load. Doing that with this unit emits an all out rotting odor. We've found the rinse feature does help a little. Cleaning the filter is relatively easy and takes about 3 minutes. We usually run the unit after dinner, have it set to automatically open the door when finished. I'll pull the drawers out and let it finish drying over night. By the next morning the dishes are all completely dry. I'd buy this unit again despite the reliance on the app. It cleans well which is the main reason. It can just be a little difficlut to get there.

Sentence (English): We bough this to replace a KitchenAid machine that never worked right and the differences are stark.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || We bough this to replace a KitchenAid machine that never worked right and the differences are stark. I've never gotten dishes this clean and dry out of a dishwasher before. Loading the top silverware rack took a little bit of an adjustment, but once we figured it out this is a much better system than the basket I've always had in American-style dishwashers. I LOVE that this doesn't use a separate heating element to dry dishes and you can put plastic anywhere. It also reminds you when it needs maintenance or when its rinse aid reservoir is empty, which didn't seem like something I'd care about until I absolutely did. Buying this dishwasher brought me more joy in the last few months that I've owned it than I ever thought an appliance could or should. Or maybe I'm just getting old — I also like gettig socks for my birthday now.

We we weary about the price point, but in this case the saying ' you get what you pay for' really does apply. Everything from the delivery to the installation of the actual product was impressive. This machine is a literal powerhouse-  I mean, it comes with wifi capability and an app?? My wife helped me with installing the app since she's the tech savvy one. I was taken back when I could see things such as the time left on the dishwasher on the app and whether or not the dishwaher was on and working. Which is helpful when you have so many other errands to do. One of the many features on this machine is its capability to actually dry! My GOD-- my dishes came out clean and dry ( who would have thought?). My wife also loves that there's a hidden treasure storage up top to place spatulas or anything else that's small and flat. In addition, we were so used to the many garbled sounds that the previous one made-- we thought all dishwashers were like that. So, when we were getting ready to watch a movie we thought we had not yet turned on the dishwasher because we literally couldnt hear anything! I knew my wife was about to yell at me to get up and make sure it was started, but then she said, ' honey, why don't you just check the app on your phone--it should tell you if it's on and running!' I thought - wow - I am living like a Jetson. I would definitely recommened splurging on this product- worth every penny!
